hero.title: Set up a fresh machine from one inspectable command.
hero.lede: The public repository contains only safe, audited configuration. It installs the baseline, authenticates GitHub locally when needed, and hands off to the private xtreemze/.dotfiles repository only for accounts that can access it.

install.title: Choose this machine
install.platformHelp: The bootstrap detects the platform automatically. This selection previews the package plan for the machine you intend to configure.
install.rolesHelp: Roles are additive. Select everything this machine should do.
install.bashNote: Uses Bash explicitly because the bootstrap relies on Bash features.
install.termuxNote: Run this inside Termux. Bash is installed as a bootstrap prerequisite if necessary.

plan.title: What gets installed
plan.description: The table combines the base, selected platform, and selected roles.

catalog.title: Every package, explained
catalog.intro: Explore the baseline, platform layers, and each role independently. Every tool includes its purpose in this setup, alternatives worth considering, and a link to the upstream project. Alternatives are informational only and are not installed.
catalog.help: Required packages are part of the minimum contract. Optional packages are attempted when available and may be skipped without making the bootstrap unusable.

trust.title: Public first. Private only after authentication.
trust.description: The public checkout lives at ~/.local/share/xtreemze/dotfiles-public. The private checkout keeps the canonical ~/.dotfiles path and is never fetched until GitHub CLI confirms access.
steps: Clone safe repository and install baseline packages.
Install gh if missing and reuse existing auth where possible.
Run gh auth login; no token is stored in this repository.
Authorized machines clone private configuration into ~/.dotfiles.
Without private access, apply only the audited public Stow packages.

policy.title: What is safe to publish
cards: Bootstrap logic, package metadata, documentation, role plans, and explicitly audited path-agnostic configuration.
Machine metadata, personal Git identity, SSH material, auth state, secrets, service credentials, private helpers, and configuration that still assumes private paths.
The publication pipeline uses an allowlist, rejects symlinks, scans for high-risk secret patterns, and validates shell entrypoints before Pages deploys.

after.title: A small command vocabulary
commands: Preview changes without modifying the machine.
Check tools, Stow links, and platform prerequisites.
after.note: just is convenience only. The installer and dotfiles CLI remain usable directly.

managed.title: Everything this repository manages
managed.intro: This inventory combines package installation and configuration ownership. It includes software installed by Homebrew or role manifests, shell and application configuration deployed with Stow, and private repository configuration that is intentionally not published.
managed.empty: No managed items match this filter.

design.title: A consistent visual and interaction language
design.intro: The repository treats presentation, typography, keyboard behavior, and controls as part of the configuration contract.
philosophyItems: Native platform conventions where they do not conflict

cloud.title: One canonical Rclone cloud surface
cloud.intro: Rclone is the authorized cloud-storage abstraction. Provider credentials stay local, while the dotfiles standardize access through cloud: and, where supported, mount it automatically at ~/Cloud.
cloud.identityBody: Any configured backend can be exposed through the canonical cloud: alias, keeping scripts and workflows provider-independent.
cloud.vfsBody: macOS uses Rclone NFS mounting; supported Linux hosts use FUSE 3. VFS full caching is enabled with bounded cache size and age.
cloud.safeBody: Credentials are never committed. Termux and hosts without filesystem mounting continue to use Rclone copy, sync, and transfer commands directly.

macos.label: macOS
macos.note: The public Brewfile is the package authority on macOS; role flags still carry forward to the authenticated private handoff.

linux.label: Linux
linux.note: The installer detects the native package manager and resolves logical package names through the public catalog.

termux.label: Termux
termux.note: Termux uses native packages only for the public baseline and keeps mobile configuration isolated from desktop assumptions.

base.label: Base
base.description: Minimum terminal foundation installed on every managed machine.
base.note: These are bootstrap and configuration-management primitives, not a user-facing workload role.

macos.label: macOS
macos.description: Public workstation package set used on macOS.
macos.note: macOS package state is driven by the public Brewfile; private setup can add sensitive or machine-specific layers after authentication.

linux.label: Linux
linux.description: Portable shell and terminal additions available through supported Linux package managers.
linux.note: Package names may map differently across apt, dnf, pacman, and apk, while the logical tool remains the same.

termux.label: Termux
termux.description: Native Termux packages for a usable mobile terminal and GitHub-authenticated handoff.
termux.note: The public path intentionally avoids uncertified downloaded binaries on Termux.

development.label: Development
development.description: Developer-oriented editor, repository, search, and runtime tooling.
development.note: This layer is additive to the base and detected platform.

desktop.label: Desktop
desktop.description: Interactive monitoring, system inspection, disk analysis, and logs for desktop/workstation machines.
desktop.note: These tools are optional conveniences and do not alter configuration authority.

server.label: Server
server.description: Small, broadly packaged tools for process inspection and remote file synchronization.
server.note: Optimized for headless hosts where graphical diagnostics are unavailable.

remote.label: Remote
remote.description: Editor, file navigation, prompt, history, jumping, and search tools for interactive remote sessions.
remote.note: Designed to make an SSH shell feel close to the local terminal experience.

mobile.label: Mobile
mobile.description: A deliberately smaller terminal experience for phones and other constrained clients.
mobile.note: Platform-specific Termux packages are shown separately from this role.

fuse3.summary: Userspace filesystem support required for mounting Rclone remotes as filesystems on Linux.
fuse3.why: Enables the automatic Rclone VFS mount on supported Linux hosts without coupling the cloud workflow to a specific provider.

managedTools.bash: Interactive shell configuration for portable aliases, completions, environment setup, and command behavior.
managedTools.fish: Fish shell configuration for interactive navigation, completions, prompt integration, and terminal tooling.
managedTools.nushell: Structured shell configuration for Nushell commands, environment behavior, and terminal integrations.
managedTools.skim: Fuzzy finder used to build fast interactive selection workflows from shell and terminal tools.
managedTools.carapace: Multi-shell completion engine used to provide richer command completions across supported shells.
managedTools.git-delta: Syntax-aware pager for Git diffs that makes review output easier to scan in the terminal.
managedTools.npm: npm client configuration for Node.js package registry and package-manager behavior.
managedTools.age: Small modern encryption tool used as part of the private secrets-management workflow.
managedTools.sops: Structured secrets editor used to keep encrypted configuration safely version-controlled.
managedTools.gitleaks: Secret scanner used to catch credentials and high-risk material before it reaches published history.
managedTools.kanata: Cross-platform keyboard remapping engine used for programmable input behavior outside application-specific shortcuts.
managedTools.ghostty: Terminal emulator whose private configuration is managed by the dotfiles repository.
managedTools.karabiner: macOS keyboard customization application with repository-managed private configuration.
managedTools.stats: macOS menu-bar system monitor for quick CPU, memory, disk, network, and sensor visibility.
managedTools.font-monaspace: Monaspace font family installed for consistent terminal and editor typography.
managedTools.ssh: Private OpenSSH client configuration for hosts, identities, connection behavior, and remote workflows.
managedTools.aws-sso: Repository-held AWS SSO configuration for authenticated cloud access; metadata is private and not publicly exported.
managedTools.oatmeal: Terminal AI client configuration managed privately for interactive command-line workflows.
managedTools.streamrip: Private streamrip configuration for command-line media retrieval workflows.
managedTools.termux-config: Termux-specific terminal settings and mobile integration configuration for Android devices.
managedTools.rclone: Authorized cloud-storage abstraction for synchronization, transfer, and automatic VFS access across managed machines.
managedTools.fuse3: Userspace filesystem support used by Rclone VFS mounts on Linux.
